newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Aug 6.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Aug 6.

text.p: The following stories were reported in Wednesday's electronic version of The Wall Street Journal.
* The Thai government said it would close half the country's finance companies.
* Aetna posted lackluster quarterly results, sending its stock down 12.0 percent.
* Cabletron founder, president and chief executive S. Robert Levine plans to resign from the company.
* United Parcel Service's proposal to set up its own pension plan that would replace a Teamsters union plan is at the heart of the union's strike against the company.
* Tech stocks soared, sending the Nasdaq to a record high, while the Dow Industrials slid and the dollar rose.
* EDS won the lead role in a multiyear $4.0 billion deal to run the computer systems of BellSouth's biggest unit.
* Cisco Systems posted a 34.0 percent rise in its quarterly profits.
* Igene sued ADM, alleging ADM stole secrets regarding Igene's process for making a pigment to turn farm-raised salmon pink.
* A New York Stock Exchange administrator is being investigated by the Manhattan's attorney's office over allegations he took bribes from brokerage firms.
* Columbia/HCA faces a separate Medicaid fraud probe by Florida officials.

* Aon is working with federal investigators to determine whether a former employee of its Alexander & Alexander unit lost as much as $27 million on speculative investments and then tried to hide the losses.
* Starwood Lodging agreed to buy three Westin Hotels for about $133 million.
* Ford said its July sales of cars and light trucks rose 5.0 percent.
* Boeing is likely to get an order for a batch of passenger planes from China before a U.S.-China presidential summitt in October.
* Viacom posted a quarterly loss of $195 million amid Blockbuster charges.
* One analyst is betting that retail stocks will see big gains in this year's second half.
* Bonds slipped as investors again feared a rise in interest rates.
